walkthrough: Substitute the expression for $f(x) = x + \frac{1}{x}$ into the function $g(x) = ax + 1$:

State the composite function expression:
$$gf(x) = a\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right) + 1$$

Substitute $x = 2$ into the composite function expression and equate to $11$:
$$a\left(2 + \frac{1}{2}\right) + 1 = 11$$

hints: Recall that a function must be one-to-one to have an inverse.
walkthrough: Determine whether $f$ has an inverse on domain $x > 0$.

Explain that $f(x)$ has a turning point at $x = 1$, making it a many-to-one function, so $f^{-1}$ does not exist:
$$\text{No, because } f(x) \text{ is not a one-to-one function}$$

Find the inverse function $g^{-1}(x)$ for $g(x) = 5x + 1$:
$$y = 5x + 1 \implies x = \frac{y - 1}{5} \implies g^{-1}(x) = \frac{x - 1}{5}$$

Combine the numerator into a single fraction and simplify:
$$g^{-1}f(x) = \frac{\frac{x^2 - x + 1}{x}}{5} = \frac{x^2 - x + 1}{5x}$$

hints: Compare the range of $g$ with the domain of $f$.
Give a specific example such as $g(-1) = -4 \le 0$.
walkthrough: Identify the range of $g(x) = 5x + 1$, which is all real numbers $\mathbb{R}$.
State that since the domain of $f$ requires $x > 0$, the range of $g$ is not a subset of the domain of $f$ (for example, $g(-1) = -4 \le 0$ which cannot be input into $f$).
